questions.q:
Question 1
Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since, the OH group increases the electron density more to $\mathrm{o}-$ and $\mathrm{p}-$ positions therefore OH group is ortho, para-directing. Reimer-Tiemann reaction is one of the examples of aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. This is a general method used for the ortho-formylation of phenols.
(a) What happens when phenol reacts with
(i) $\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{CS}_2$
(ii) Conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$
(b) Why phenol does not undergo protonation readily?
(c) Which is a stronger acid - phenol or cresol ? Give reason.
Question 2
(c) Write the IUPAC name of the product formed in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
questions.solution:
Question 1
Solution: (a)
(i)

/ 2-Bromophenol and 4-Bromophenol is formed.
(ii)

/ 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol / Picric acid is formed.
(b) Due to resonance, the lone pair of electrons on oxygen is not easily available for protonation.
(c) Phenol

questions.q:
Question 1
Alcohols undergo a number of reactions involving the cleavage of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}$ bond. However, phenols do not undergo reactions involving the cleavage of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}$ bond. Alcohols are weaker acids than water. Alcohols react with halogen acids to form the corresponding haloalkanes. Phenols are stronger acids than alcohols. A characteristic feature of phenols is that they undergo electrophilic substitution reactions such as halogenation, nitration, etc. Since - OH group is a strong activating group, phenol gives trisubstituted products during halogenation, nitration, etc.
(a) What happens when phenol is treated with the following?
(i) $\mathrm{Br}_2$ water
(ii) Conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$

Alcohols undergo a number of reactions involving the cleavage of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}$ bond. However, phenols do not undergo reactions involving the cleavage of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}$ bond.
